title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Ava Martinez
description: Brings Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions closer to parity with the public API. Motivation: customers are switching apps that rely on nuanced chat parameters (roles, stop sequences, logprobs) and streaming semantics; several downstream SDKs and examples expect identical parameter handling and response shape. This PR implements: 1) parameter normalization for 'temperature', 'top_p', 'presence_penalty', 'frequency_penalty', and legacy 'n' handling to match OpenAI semantics; 2) robust 'roles' handling so assistant/system/user roles map deterministically to our internal chat format (preserves role ordering and role-specific parsing); 3) stop-sequence support with streaming-aware truncation and early termination hooks; 4) optional 'logprobs' support for sampling endpoints with a consistent field format in both streaming and non-streaming responses; 5) response formatting fixes so 'choices[].message' matches OpenAI keys, and function/tool-calling payloads keep 'name' + 'arguments' formatting; 6) added comprehensive test vectors and e2e tests against the openai-compat harness. Backwards compatible where possible; feature-gated logprobs to avoid perf regressions on default paths. Checklist: - [x] parameter normalization implemented - [x] roles ordering deterministic - [x] stop sequence streaming termination - [x] logprobs serialization + feature flag - [x] response formatting and function call payload parity - [x] unit tests and integration tests - [x] docs updated (openai-compat.md) Links: Linear ENG-8934, internal design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8934/openai-chat-completions-parity
commits: normalize: map openai chat params to runtime config
streaming: early stop hook for stop sequences
roles: preserve ordering and canonicalize role names
logprobs: add optional sampling metadata serialization (feature-flagged)
tests: add openai-compat e2e vectors and unit tests
docs: update openai-compat.md with examples and caveats
change_snippets: // params_mapper.rs: map 'n' to parallel streams when n > 1, else single response
// stop_handler.rs: if streaming and stop matched, emit final token and send 'done' sentinel to SSE
// logprobs_serializer: attach 'logprobs' map only when feature flag ENABLE_LOGPROBS=true to avoid perf cost
review_comments: Liam: Can we confirm that stop sequences containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters are handled correctly in streaming? I saw a failing unit test on my machine.

Ava: Yes — added explicit byte-boundary-aware matching and test vector for multibyte stops in tests/integration/openai_chat_parity.test.yaml. The failing test was due to a stale fixture; CI now passes.

Priya: We're returning 'choices[].message.content' for non-function replies but for function calls we need 'choices[].message.role' == 'assistant' and 'choices[].message.function_call' shape to exactly match OpenAI. Please add a regression test.
Ava: Added structured-output example and integration test verifying function_call.name and function_call.arguments are present and quoted exactly as OpenAI does.
Marcus: logprobs path looks expensive. Feature-flag seems fine, but add a note in the docs about performance tradeoffs and recommended sampling settings.
Ava: Added performance guidance in docs/openai-compat.md and added a unit test that asserts the logprobs serializer is skipped when the flag is off.
ci_checks: benchmarks: baseline run (no regressions within 2% on p90 latency)
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility improvements: param mapping (temperature, top_p, penalties), deterministic role ordering, streaming-aware stop sequence handling, optional logprobs support (feature-flag), and response formatting fixes for function/tool calling. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration notes.
summary: Parity work for OpenAI chat.completions: ensures request params and response shapes match OpenAI so clients using openai-compat have minimal migration friction. Improves streaming stability for stop sequences and preserves role semantics; logprobs are behind a feature flag to avoid default perf impact.
